---
title: Call an external service
description: Make one HTTPS request from a method that writes, with a secret the node fills in, and know every gate a node puts in front of it.
sidebar:
  order: 6.2
---

import { Aside, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

**Task:** call a service outside the network — a captcha check, a payment
API, a model, any HTTPS API — and write what it answers into state.

A run may ask its node for **one** HTTPS request. The node makes it only when
every gate below holds and answers with its reason otherwise. Outbound requests
are **off on every node by default**: an app that needs them runs only on nodes
whose operator turned them on, for its hosts or for any host an app declares.

## The gates

| Gate | Who sets it |
| --- | --- |
| `[context.outbound] enabled = true`, and the request's host is in `hosts` (or `hosts` holds `"*"`: any host an installed app declares) | The node's operator |
| The request's URL is under a prefix in the app's signed manifest (`outbound`): the same host, and the prefix's path or one below it at a `/`, with any query string | The app's publisher |
| The run writes state and executes on this node, as its own write or one it relays for an author: not a view, a migration, a state op or a peer's delta | The node |
| One request per run; `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`; `https` on port 443 to a DNS name that resolves only to public addresses; no fragment; no redirect followed; no proxy | The node |
| Request body ≤ 64 KiB, URL ≤ 2 KiB, ≤ 8 headers of ≤ 1 KiB, response body ≤ 1 MiB (a longer one is refused, not cut), 10 s for the whole request | The node (`calimero_primitives::outbound`) |
| `Host`, `Cookie`, `Connection`, `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Proxy-*` and `X-Forwarded-*` headers are refused | The node |

A refusal is a reason the method can handle (`Err(String)`). A run with no
outbound client at all (the node's feature is off, the manifest declares
nothing, or the run is a view) and a second request in one run trap the run.

## Secrets

The app never holds a secret. A request names one as `{{secret:NAME}}` in a
header value or the body; the node fills it in from **its operator's**
secrets, for this app only (the package and signer of the installed bundle,
never anything the app says), and only into a request to a host the operator
bound that secret to. Any copy of it in the response is replaced with
`[redacted]` before the app sees the response. So a method cannot write the
secret into state, where it would replicate to every member.

<Steps>

1. Declare the URL prefixes in `Cargo.toml`. They are signed into the
   bundle's manifest and shown at install, so declare the narrowest that
   works:

   ```toml
   [package.metadata.calimero]
   outbound = [
     "https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify",
     "https://api.stripe.com/v1/",   # every path below /v1/
   ]
   ```

2. Make the request from a method that writes, and store the decision:

   ```rust
   use calimero_sdk::env;
   use calimero_sdk::outbound::{OutboundMethod, OutboundRequest};

   pub fn submit(&mut self, answer: String, captcha_token: String) -> app::Result<()> {
       let response = env::http_request(&OutboundRequest {
           method: OutboundMethod::Post,
           url: "https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify".to_owned(),
           headers: vec![(
               "Content-Type".to_owned(),
               "application/x-www-form-urlencoded".to_owned(),
           )],
           body: format!("secret={{{{secret:TURNSTILE_SECRET}}}}&response={captcha_token}")
               .into_bytes(),
       })
       .map_err(|reason| app::err!("captcha check failed: {reason}"))?;
       if response.status != 200 || !String::from_utf8_lossy(&response.body).contains(r#""success":true"#) {
           app::bail!("captcha not solved");
       }
       self.answers.push(answer.into())?;
       Ok(())
   }
   ```

3. On the node, allow the host and supply the secret (see
   [the operator's side](#the-operators-side)).

</Steps>

<Aside type="caution" title="Only the executing node asks">
The request runs once, on the node that executes the method. Peers apply the
resulting delta; they never repeat the request and never see its response.
Store the decision, not the response, and do not make a write depend on a
second node agreeing with the first.
</Aside>

## The operator's side

`[context.outbound]` in the node's `config.toml`:

```toml
[context.outbound]
enabled = true
hosts = ["challenges.cloudflare.com", "api.stripe.com"]   # or ["*"]

# Secrets from environment variables, read once at start: a missing one
# fails the start.
[context.outbound.env_secrets.TURNSTILE_SECRET]
env = "MERO_TURNSTILE_SECRET"
packages = ["com.calimero.mero-forms"]
signers = ["did:key:z6Mk…"]   # the bundle's signerId
hosts = ["challenges.cloudflare.com"]
```

`hosts = ["*"]` lets every installed app reach the hosts its own signed
manifest declares, so a new app needs no config change. Every other gate
still holds, and a secret still goes only to the hosts bound to it.

Instead of `env_secrets`, a node can ask a secrets service beside it
(exclusive with `env_secrets`):

```toml
[context.outbound.sidecar]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:7070/v1/secret"
token_env = "MERO_SECRETS_TOKEN"
```

The node `POST`s `{"package", "signer", "name"}` with the token as a bearer and
expects `200 {"value", "hosts"}` or `404`. The URL must be `http` on a loopback
address. A managed deployment answers there with the secrets a deployer set
for their app, for every namespace that runs it, so the secret lives on the
nodes that serve the app and nowhere else.

The node logs every request it makes or refuses, with the context, the app
and the URL, never the secret.

A secret is matched on both the package and the bundle's signer: anyone can
name a package, only its publisher can sign it.

## Where it stops

- A request never runs in a view. Read the answer back from state.
- Members who run the app on their own node need outbound requests on
  there too, or their writes that call `http_request` trap. Route those writes
  to a node that has them (a relay or a TEE).
- Redaction removes the secret as sent. A service that answers with it
  encoded (base64, URL-escaped) defeats it, so bind a secret only to hosts that
  do not echo it.
- The response is not authenticated beyond TLS: a service you call can answer
  anything, so call only services you trust for the decision you store.
